options_evaluated: Monomaterial post-consumer recycled polypropylene (PCR-PP) without overmolding
Multi-layered co-extruded plastics with soft-touch elastomer overmolding
assessments.recommendation: Monomaterial post-consumer recycled polypropylene (PCR-PP) without overmolding
assessments.rationale: According to ESPR Annex I parameters (d) ease and quality of recycling, and (e) avoidance of solutions detrimental to recycling, monomaterial construction is critical. Avoiding elastomer overmolding and fiber reinforcements prevents contamination of the polymer recycling stream, ensuring high-quality mechanical recycling. This also reduces the generation of microplastics (p) during shredding and minimizes overall end-of-life waste (r).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing (PCR-PP may have higher processing variability and lower yield rates) and Product Use/Performance (lack of overmolding and fiber reinforcement reduces impact resistance and structural rigidity, and may increase acoustic noise transmission).

options_evaluated: Reversible mechanical fasteners (standardized screws and snap-fits)
assessments.recommendation: Reversible mechanical fasteners (standardized screws and snap-fits)
assessments.rationale: Aligned with ESPR Annex I parameters (c) ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing and refurbishment, and (d) ease of recycling. Reversible fasteners allow non-destructive disassembly of the vacuum cleaner, enabling components to be harvested for reuse or remanufacturing. It avoids the use of adhesives or welds which contaminate material fractions, thus preventing solutions detrimental to recovery (e) and reducing end-of-life waste (r).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing (increased assembly time, higher part count, and higher production costs) and Product Use/Performance (potential for air leaks at joints over time due to vibration, reducing suction efficiency).

options_evaluated: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor designed for non-destructive magnet and bearing extraction
Standard BLDC motor with glued rare-earth magnets
Conventional brushed AC motor with integrated non-replaceable carbon brushes
assessments.recommendation: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor designed for non-destructive magnet and bearing extraction
assessments.rationale: In line with ESPR Annex I parameters (c) ease of remanufacturing and refurbishment, and (d) ease and quality of recycling. Standard BLDC motors glue rare-earth magnets to the rotor, making recovery economically unviable. Designing the motor for non-destructive disassembly allows high-value neodymium magnets and copper windings to be recovered cleanly, reducing the environmental footprint of end-of-life treatment (m) and avoiding resource-intensive pyrometallurgical processing (g).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing (more complex motor design and higher initial manufacturing cost) and Product Use/Performance (mechanical retention of magnets may slightly reduce motor power density or maximum rotational speed compared to adhesive bonding).

options_evaluated: Passive cooling via optimized airflow channels and mechanically attached aluminum heatsinks
Active cooling with dedicated auxiliary fans and phase-change materials
Potting and encapsulation of electronics in thermally conductive epoxy resins
assessments.recommendation: Passive cooling via optimized airflow channels and mechanically attached aluminum heatsinks
assessments.rationale: Grounded in ESPR Annex I parameters (d) ease and quality of recycling, and (e) avoidance of solutions detrimental to reuse, recycling, or recovery. Potting or encapsulating electronics in epoxy resins permanently bonds the components, making component-level repair/refurbishment (c) impossible and rendering the PCB completely unrecyclable. Mechanical heatsinks can be easily detached, allowing clean separation of aluminum and electronic scrap, reducing EOL waste (r).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Product Use/Performance (risk of higher operating temperatures under heavy load, potentially reducing electronic component lifespan) and Acoustics (passive cooling may require larger airflow vents, increasing noise emissions).

options_evaluated: Fully modular architecture with tool-accessible, independent sub-assemblies
Semi-modular design with integrated motor-impeller units
Monolithic integrated architecture with hardwired components
assessments.recommendation: Fully modular architecture with tool-accessible, independent sub-assemblies
assessments.rationale: Directly supports ESPR Annex I parameters (c) ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing and refurbishment, and (r) amounts of waste generated. A modular architecture allows individual high-wear parts (such as the motor, cord reel, or switch assembly) to be replaced or refurbished independently. This prevents the entire vacuum cleaner from being discarded due to a single component failure, drastically reducing waste (r) and EOL resource consumption (g).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Manufacturing (requires more connectors, housing partitions, and structural support, increasing weight and material costs) and Product Use/Performance (increased overall product weight and volume).

options_evaluated: Removable, modular Li-ion battery pack with toolless release and non-glued cell construction
Corded AC power supply with integrated non-replaceable cord reel
assessments.recommendation: Removable, modular Li-ion battery pack with toolless release and non-glued cell construction
assessments.rationale: Grounded in ESPR Annex I parameters (c) ease of upgrading, reuse, remanufacturing and refurbishment, (d) ease and quality of recycling, and (m) environmental footprint in end-of-life treatment. Batteries are the most common point of failure in cordless appliances. A toolless, removable pack prevents premature product disposal (r). Non-glued cell construction allows safe disassembly for cell-level testing, repair, or high-yield recycling of lithium, cobalt, and nickel without energy-intensive thermal treatment (g).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Product Use/Performance (cordless vacuums have limited run times and lower suction power than corded alternatives; a modular battery pack also adds weight and bulk) and Manufacturing (higher cost of specialized battery management systems and robust mechanical locking interfaces).
